title: Anthropic Defends Cowork Cloud Shift for Battery and Mobile Access
summary:
An employee on the Cowork team said that transitioning virtual machine processing to company servers was essential to reduce resource strain on local hardware. Felix Rieseberg, who works on the tool, stated that this shift ends the disk, battery, and performance costs of running a VM locally and enables the product to be used on smartphones. He noted that while Pro and Max subscribers received email and in-app notifications about the change, the transition was more surprising to the user base than he would have liked.

The new architecture utilizes isolated sandboxes for each session that are destroyed after the session ends. To access local files, the desktop application now manages specific tool calls for folders that the user has explicitly authorized. This response follows criticism from users who argue that cloud compute is insufficient for multimedia workloads, as Anthropic recently removed the local execution option for its highest subscription tiers.

selectedTweets.bestBit: People loved what they were able to do with Claude but didn't love the disk, battery, and performance cost of running the VM locally
selectedTweets.text:
@GergelyOrosz Hi! I work on Cowork. Probably no surprise, but we want to make our users as powerful as possible with Claude - and you're right that explaining and keeping up with the capabilities is hard. Affected users got both an email and an in-app notice, but I'm grateful for the feedback - I think this change was more surprising to people than I'd like it to be. This one will be a longer explainer, bear with me!

The "old" version of Cowork runs model inference in the cloud, executing tool calls in an Anthropic-provided VM we shipped to your computer. We added the VM for capability, safety, and security reasons - mapping in just the data you explicitly added to your session. People loved what they were able to do with Claude but didn't love the disk, battery, and performance cost of running the VM locally. Also, people didn't love that closing your laptop means the work stops.

The "new" version of Cowork runs model inference and the VM in the cloud. Each session gets its own sandbox, not sharing state with other sessions. When the VM needs something on the users' device (like a file), the desktop app is responsible for that file access tool call. To be clear, Claude will only access files in folders that the user explicitly added to the session, the same way Claude only saw files explicitly added to the VM in the "old" version. Sandboxes are destroyed when the session ends!

We think this solves a lot of problems we've heard about  (like using Cowork from a phone, keeping work running, or getting all the same power without losing battery to the VM) - but we'll keep iterating on new feedback we hear!
